data.narrative:
Vast is a late-stage space & aerospace company founded by Jed McCaleb that has raised $300M+ to date. The valuation landscape includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though the broader sector contains 14 same-sector entities.

Only the stage-progression method proves applicable here. Using total raised ($300M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage advancement yields $360M implied value. Peer-median triangulation cannot proceed due to insufficient data points within tight same-stage and similar-tier filters—while 14 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three meet narrow comparability criteria. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 27.4x across five tickers) cannot be applied without Vast's disclosed revenue, which is not on file.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $306M to $414M, with a median of $360M. This range should be treated as illustrative rather than definitive given reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure, which prevents calibration against public multiples, and sparse late-stage comparable data in the space sector. Any valuation update would benefit from either disclosed revenue metrics or identification of additional late-stage private space companies with known valuations.
